info.desc: Tubular Bells is a record album, written and mostly performed by Mike Oldfield, released in 1973. The late Vivian Stanshall provided the voice of the "Master of Ceremonies" who reads off the list of instruments at the end of the first movement. The piece was later orchestrated by David Bedford for The Orchestral Tubular Bells version and it had two sequels in the 1990s, Tubular Bells II and Tubular Bells III. Significance Oldfield approached (and was rejected by) many other established record labels. Some of the rejections were because they believed the piece to be unmarketable. podcast.body: Mike Oldfield's "Tubular Bells" was the first signing and release for Virgin Records, proving to be a huge hit. Its commercial success provided Virgin with the necessary funds to finance its expansion. "So Branson and his partners did, and their first signing was 2-biter bells by Mike Oldfield. That became a huge hit which allowed Virgin to finance an expansion."

podcast.body: The title track from this 1974 album was so extensive it had to be split across both sides of the vinyl record. Part one ran for 25 minutes and 36 seconds on side one, while part two took up 23 minutes and 20 seconds on side two, making it technically not a single, unbroken piece of music. "Its title track was so long that it had to be divided into two. Part one ran 25 minutes and 36 seconds on side one. Well, part two took up 23 minutes and 20 seconds on side two."

podcast.body: This album, released in 1973, revolutionized the music industry. Its immense success was pivotal for the foundation and growth of Virgin Records, contributing significantly to Richard Branson's fortune as it was the breakthrough hit for his nascent record label, which had started in the early 1970s. "todos lo conocemos porque en 1973 sacaba el grandísimo tubular bells con el que revolucionaba la industria de la música."
